title: Design map readable: no label over a node, audit can fail
requirement: The owner requires the Design map to be visually readable: elements must not overlap each other (labels over nodes, labels over labels, edges through nodes), the map must be expressive and legible in the panel's light and dark themes, and a visual-consistency check must exist instead of silently emitting a broken map.
steps: Render the repository map and the fixtures/readability dense (20 nodes), cyclic and multiline views through core (renderView).

Run bin/audit-scene.mjs on each view and on the pre-fix harness scenes: the new views report 0 collisions and exit 0; harness/scenes/m0 and harness/scenes/fixture report 4 and 3 labels over nodes and exit 1.
Move a rendered plate inside a node and run the audit again: it reports label_over_node and exits 1 (negative control).
Check the panel in a browser at 1280x720 and 1440x900 in light and dark themes: label chips, theme canvas, real zoom, legend counts.
expected: Every rendered view has zero collisions (label plate over a node, two plates over each other, edge body through a node), zero plates outside the canvas; the audit exits 0 on the demo and readability fixtures and exits 1 on the pre-fix harness scenes and on a scene whose plate is moved inside a node. A layout that cannot place a plate refuses render with label_collision instead of emitting the overlapping scene.
